title: Pop Culture Digest — Sunday, October 25, 2026
description:
Sunday · October 25, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Sunday’s conversation: Jay-Z closing his 30th-anniversary run with Snoop Dogg and Dr. Dre at SoFi, Quentin Tarantino springing the first 17 minutes of David Fincher’s Cliff Booth on an AFI Fest crowd, and Alexander Skarsgård’s woven husband in Wicker turning into an IKEA ad and a box office surprise.
Music

Jay-Z closes his anniversary tour with Snoop Dogg, Dr. Dre and Too Short

The final “Jay-Z 30” show at SoFi Stadium Saturday night leaned hard into the West Coast. Too Short came out early for “Blow the Whistle,” and later Snoop Dogg and Dr. Dre ran through “Nuthin’ but a ‘G’ Thang,” “Still D.R.E.,” “The Next Episode” and “California Love.” Jay-Z also paid tribute to Nipsey Hussle, calling him “Nip the great.” “Tonight is special,” he told the crowd.

That wraps a yearlong celebration of Reasonable Doubt’s 30th anniversary that ran through Yankee Stadium, London and Paris. SoFi hosts the Super Bowl in February, and Variety framed the two shows as a possible test run amid talk that Jay-Z could be the halftime act, though nothing was announced from the stage.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   USA Today →

Movies

Tarantino surprises AFI Fest with the first 17 minutes of Cliff Booth

After a Once Upon a Time … in Hollywood Q&A at the TCL Chinese Theatre Friday night, Tarantino told the crowd, “I could talk a little bit about The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, or I could show you the first 17 minutes.” It was the first public look at the sequel, which he wrote and David Fincher directed, with Brad Pitt back as the stuntman, now working as a Hollywood fixer in 1977. Early reactions called it darker and more psychological than the original.

Fincher has said he cut 60 pages from a 230-page script and the final film runs about two and a half hours. It opens in IMAX on Nov. 25 and streams on Netflix Dec. 23. Tarantino also talked up his first stage play, The Popinjay Cavalier, starring Sacha Baron Cohen in London’s West End next spring.

Cliff Booth trailer on YouTube →   ·   Deadline →

Movies

The internet’s Wicker obsession turns into a $6 million opening

Alexander Skarsgård plays a basket-woven fantasy husband made for Olivia Colman’s lonely fisherwoman, and clips of the movie’s sex scenes went viral so fast that IKEA posted a rattan bench “made from husband material.” Skarsgård told AFP the Weta Workshop suit was heavy and glued to his face, so his first reaction was “panic and claustrophobia,” and he had to exaggerate every expression to read through it.

The buzz is paying off. Black Bear’s period comedy, also starring Peter Dinklage and Elizabeth Debicki, made $2.36 million Friday and is heading for a $5.5–6 million opening at 1,471 theaters, with an audience that’s 79% women and strong exit polls.

Wicker trailer on YouTube →   ·   TheWrap →   ·   Deadline →

Bottom of the news

  • Clayface is heading for a $24–25 million No. 1 opening with an A- CinemaScore, and You Can See Everything is up as much as 28% in its second weekend at $19–20 million.
  • Laika’s Wildwood earned an A CinemaScore on an $11 million start, while Taika Waititi’s Klara and the Sun is opening to about $725,000.
  • Kim Kardashian, Naomi Watts and Sarah Paulson premiered All’s Fair season 2 at the Rome Film Festival.
  • Dakota Johnson and Machine Gun Kelly were spotted out together in Los Angeles again, fueling romance rumors.
  • The Challenge and Real World star Anika Rashaun died of breast cancer at 34.
  • Taylor Swift’s The Life of a Showgirl logged a 15th week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
  • SNL aired a rerun Saturday; it returns Oct. 31 with Obsession star Inde Navarrette hosting and Gracie Abrams as musical guest.
